_note: Check registry — the single source of truth for what Citely measures. Analyzers emit a state per check id; _scoring.py turns states into scores. Thresholds live HERE (not in analyzer code) so they are auditable and tunable in one place. 24 checks, 6 per category: engagement sits at exact parity with discoverability, per the rubric's 'across both discoverability and engagement'.

_field_reference.id: Stable identifier. Never reuse or renumber — findings and tests reference it.
_field_reference.category: One of the four scoring categories.
_field_reference.weight: Relative weight WITHIN its category. Weights per category sum to 100.
_field_reference.confidence_class: verified = directly observed fact; heuristic = inference. Inherited by emitted findings as `confidence`.
_field_reference.kind: structural = binary/language-independent, near-zero false-positive risk. statistical = threshold-dependent, biased toward partial/unknown near the boundary.
_field_reference.depends_on: Prerequisite check ids. If a prerequisite FAILS, this check becomes `unknown` (not `fail`) — collapsing correlated findings. Anti-dodge rule: suppression only applies when the failed prerequisite is confidence_class `verified`.
_field_reference.requires_language: true = needs confident, supported page-language detection. Otherwise resolves to `unknown`, never `fail` (prevents mass false positives on non-English sites).
_field_reference.threshold: Measured values compared against these. null = purely structural presence check.
_field_reference.title: Short finding title.
_field_reference.signal: The mechanism being measured (first link of the reasoning chain).
_field_reference.impact: Why it matters for AI ingestion or human retention.
_field_reference.plain_summary: Non-expert phrasing for the report's layer-1 verdict.

checks.title: Page returns a successful HTTP status
checks.signal: HTTP status of the final URL after redirects
checks.impact: A non-2xx response means no AI crawler can ingest the page at all; every downstream signal is unmeasurable.
checks.plain_summary: AI assistants can load your page.

checks.title: robots.txt permits the AI assistants' crawlers
checks.signal: robots.txt directives evaluated for each major AI crawler user-agent (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended, CCBot, OAI-SearchBot) on the target path
checks.impact: This is the single most direct way to be invisible to AI assistants. A site can be fully crawlable by search engines yet block GPTBot, in which case ChatGPT can never read or cite it. The block is often a CDN or platform default the site owner never consciously chose.
checks.plain_summary: The AI assistants' crawlers are allowed to read your site.
checks._note: Deliberately evaluated for the AI crawlers, NOT for CitelyAuditBot. Whether OUR bot may fetch is an operational gate handled by the orchestrator (stop + partial_reason 'blocked'), not a scored check — nobody blocks an unknown auditor UA, so scoring that would pass on every site and miss real AI-crawler blocks.

checks.title: Page is not marked noindex
checks.signal: meta name=robots content and the X-Robots-Tag response header
checks.impact: A noindex directive tells engines not to retain the page, so its facts never enter the index AI systems draw on.
checks.plain_summary: Your page is not telling search engines to ignore it.

threshold._note: This check measures JS-DEPENDENCE, not thinness. Above min_visible_chars_raw the page passes outright. Below it, we only fail when there is positive evidence that JavaScript is responsible (empty mount node, framework markers, or a large render gain) or when the page is below empty_floor_chars (50) and therefore effectively blank. The floor is deliberately low: a small-but-real page (a local business homepage of ~80 characters) is thin, not JavaScript-dependent, and flagging it here would be a false positive. A short but genuinely server-rendered page is NOT a rendering defect — sparse content is judged by the information-density check instead.

checks.title: Meaningful content exists without JavaScript
checks.signal: Visible text length in the raw (pre-JavaScript) HTML response
checks.impact: Crawlers that do not execute JavaScript see an empty shell. Facts that only appear after hydration are invisible to them, so nothing is quotable or citable.
checks.plain_summary: Your content is in the page itself, not built later by the browser.

checks.title: Semantic HTML landmarks present
checks.signal: Presence of main/article/header/nav landmarks and a single h1
checks.impact: Semantic structure tells extractors which text is primary content versus navigation and boilerplate.
checks.plain_summary: Your page structure marks out what the main content is.

checks.title: Key facts are not locked inside images
checks.signal: Ratio of images carrying apparent factual content (numbers, claims) with no equivalent text or alt
checks.impact: Text baked into images, SVG or canvas cannot be parsed into embeddings, so those facts are unavailable for citation even though a human can read them.
checks.plain_summary: Your important facts are written as text, not trapped in pictures.

checks.title: Descriptive page title
checks.signal: Length and presence of the document title element
checks.impact: The title is the strongest single hint an AI summarizer uses to decide what a page is about.
checks.plain_summary: Your page title clearly says what the page is.

checks.title: Meta description present and usable
checks.signal: Presence and length of meta name=description
checks.impact: Provides a ready-made summary that answer engines frequently reuse verbatim.
checks.plain_summary: Your page has a short summary engines can reuse.

checks.title: Logical heading hierarchy
checks.signal: Heading level sequence (h1 to h6) checked for skipped levels and multiple h1s
checks.impact: Headings define the document outline summarizers use to decide which sections survive condensation.
checks.plain_summary: Your headings are in a sensible order.

checks.title: Facts presented in scannable blocks
checks.signal: Presence of lists, tables or definition lists carrying factual content
checks.impact: Structured blocks are extracted far more reliably than the same facts buried in prose paragraphs.
checks.plain_summary: Key details appear in lists or tables, not only in paragraphs.

checks.title: Self-contained, quotable factual statements
checks.signal: Count of sentences that state a complete fact without needing surrounding context
checks.impact: Retrieval systems cite sentences that stand alone. Statements that depend on the previous paragraph get dropped.
checks.plain_summary: Your page makes clear standalone statements an AI can quote.

checks.title: Information density survives summarization
checks.signal: Ratio of concrete factual sentences to total sentences, weighted by page length
checks.impact: When a summarizer condenses a long page, low-density facts surrounded by filler are the first thing discarded.
checks.plain_summary: Your key facts are not diluted by filler text.

checks.title: Structured data is present
checks.signal: Presence of parseable JSON-LD, microdata or RDFa
checks.impact: Without structured data an AI must infer identity from prose, which is where mistaken-identity and hallucination begin.
checks.plain_summary: Your page includes machine-readable information about itself.

checks.title: An organization or person entity is declared
checks.signal: A schema.org entity of an accepted identity type in the structured data graph
checks.impact: This is the anchor that tells an AI who the page is about. Without it the brand has no declared identity to attach facts to.
checks.plain_summary: Your page states who you are in a way machines understand.

checks.title: sameAs cross-references present
checks.signal: sameAs property on the declared entity
checks.impact: sameAs links let an AI corroborate identity across the web instead of guessing between similarly named entities.
checks.plain_summary: You link out to your other official profiles.

checks.title: At least one sameAs points to an authority node
checks.signal: sameAs targets matched against known authority domains
checks.impact: Corroboration needs an anchor an AI already trusts. Links only to your own properties leave the identity chain unanchored.
checks.plain_summary: At least one of your links points somewhere authoritative.

checks.title: Open Graph identity tags present
checks.signal: Presence of core og: properties
checks.impact: Open Graph is a widely consumed secondary identity signal and a fallback when JSON-LD is absent or malformed.
checks.plain_summary: Your page has social/preview tags describing it.

checks.title: Entity naming is internally consistent
checks.signal: Entity name compared across JSON-LD blocks, Open Graph site name and the document title
checks.impact: Contradictory names across blocks actively teach an AI the wrong association and are worse than no data at all.
checks.plain_summary: Your brand name is stated the same way everywhere on the page.

checks.title: A heading appears in the first viewport
checks.signal: Presence of an h1 or hero heading within the first viewport height
checks.impact: A visitor arriving from an AI answer has seconds to confirm they landed in the right place. No heading means no confirmation.
checks.plain_summary: Visitors see a clear headline as soon as they land.

checks.title: A primary action is available above the fold
checks.signal: An anchor or button element positioned within the first viewport
checks.impact: Without an obvious next step, AI-referred visitors read once and leave rather than converting.
checks.plain_summary: There is something obvious to click when visitors arrive.

checks.title: First-paint content is not obstructed
checks.signal: Full-viewport overlays, modals or consent interstitials covering initial content
checks.impact: An interstitial covering the first screen hides the very answer the visitor arrived for.
checks.plain_summary: No popup covers your content the moment visitors arrive.

checks.title: Mobile viewport is declared
checks.signal: Presence of meta name=viewport
checks.impact: Most AI-referred traffic is mobile. Without a viewport declaration the page renders unusably small.
checks.plain_summary: Your page is set up to display properly on phones.

checks.title: A value proposition is stated above the fold
checks.signal: Above-the-fold text evaluated for an action plus an offering
checks.impact: Visitors who cannot tell what you do within the first screen bounce regardless of how accurate the AI citation was.
checks.plain_summary: Visitors can tell what you offer without scrolling.

checks.title: Body text is legible
checks.signal: Computed or declared body font size
checks.impact: Text below roughly 14px is difficult to read on mobile, increasing bounce for AI-referred visitors.
checks.plain_summary: Your body text is big enough to read comfortably.
